newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN FARMERS SELLING STOCK DUE TO DROUGHT.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN FARMERS SELLING STOCK DUE TO DROUGHT.

text.p: The Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) was facing a major drought problem with farmers now selling off stock because of insufficient fodder, NSW Farmers Association president Ian Donges said in a statement.
Much of the state was in desperate need of persistent rainfall over several days, he said.
For the sixth consecutive week, yardings at cattle sales topped 20,000 head statewide because of failure of rain to fall in warmer months and generate pasture for winter feed, he said.
"A lot of farmers are engaged in expensive hand feeding at present to keep stock alive," he said.
In the north of the state, good rains early in the year lifted soil moisture levels so crops and pastures were far better than elsewhere, he said.
Most parts of the central and southern grain belt desperately needed rain, he said.
"If no decent rains come in the next couple of weeks, farmers may sacrifice their crops by letting livestock eat them to survive," he said.
However, the patchiness of rain meant there were some areas far better off than others, he said.
Excess supplies of meat onto the market had not yet seen prices fall away because of strong export demand, mainly from South Korea and Japan, he said.
Continued drought conditions would see prices ease at saleyards, he said.
NSW produced a A$2 billion grain crop last season, but was unlikely to come close to that this year, Donges said.
